title: Root Beer and Roasted Pepper Barbecue Glaze
description: A short root beer reduction brings a spiced sweetness to a smooth roasted pepper and tomato barbecue glaze.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: regular caffeine-free root beer
ingredients.note: Full-sugar, nonalcoholic soda, measured after the foam subsides.

ingredients.name: peeled roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.note: Plain and unsalted, skin and seeds removed.

steps.title: Reduce the root beer
steps.text: Pour {soda} into the HexClad. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 5–8 minutes, until reduced to about half its original volume.

steps.title: Cook the pepper base
steps.text: Whisk {tomato} into the reduction and add {pepper}, {broth} and {vinegar}. Simmer gently for 4 minutes.

steps.title: Puree the glaze
steps.text: Blend until smooth in a deep jug, then pass through a sieve back into the skillet.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the glaze over pork or chicken just before serving. For extra sauce, whisk the glaze into an already thickened mild gravy.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Reduce the root beer the day before and refrigerate until you are ready to cook the peppers. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The smooth pepper puree keeps its body for up to 2 months frozen. Whisk while reheating. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses tomato paste and vinegar. For gentler Option B, replace the tomato paste with plain butternut squash puree and use broth in place of the vinegar. The glaze is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 18 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 4.2 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 7 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment.
